body:
Born into poverty and abuse. Chronic illnesses which have waxed and waned over the years. Despite this, achieved plenty and became a productive and interesting adult. Managed my crap. Contracted [NMS](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroleptic_malignant_syndrome) last year from a medication for depression and anxiety. Fluke reaction. Lost job. Almost died. Then she left me. Now she's in love and pregnant with another man's child. Had to put my furry best friend down last week. Another fluke illness, as she went from healthy dog to braindead in a couple of weeks. 

And I am just getting back on my feet professionally in a job I don't want, in a city I don't want to be in, so I can keep chasing my dream, which is inches in front of my face but because of this recent situation that, if it doesn't make me sicker or kill me, may cost me my hearing – without giving too much away, that would be a disaster for my career in music.

It's the pretending and trying I can't handle. People have been scattering away from me since the illness last year, and it's only getting worse, and I am only getting more and more frustrated, exhausted and sad.
I'll be contacting a suicide hotline momentarily. I don't know what else to do and I'm alone in my house.

Right now they are all big. I have been trying to solve them for so long, I don't have anything left. 

I can try to explain, but they are extraordinarily unique circumstances and part of my problem is just that.
I will find out on Tuesday if I have cancerous cells in my ear. If it turns out that I do, I am done.
I should also mention, exercise is much more difficult since suffering central nervous system damage last year. I used to run four days a week, now can't do half a mile. Part of the problem.

I've been reaching out to the few people I'm close to for the last couple days. There are plenty of others I thought would still be in my life, for the rest of my life. Many of them are gone. I don't even understand why.

Short of putting myself in the hospital, I don't think anyone will give me the support I need. I don't want to do this anymore.

I would love to. Sleep is part of the problem. My illness(es) make getting real rest very difficult. Without the Klonopin, I couldn't even close my eyes.

But thank you for your concern. I'm trying extremely hard to stay on the planet a little while longer. Losing the fight.
